chapters.name: A camera that watches your back
chapters.narration: Posture Guard is a Linux desktop posture corrector. It watches you through an Intel RealSense depth camera, scores how you sit, and nudges you before the slump becomes the afternoon.

cues.text: Posture Guard is a Linux desktop posture corrector.
It watches you through an Intel RealSense depth camera, scores how you sit, and nudges you before the slump becomes the afternoon.

chapters.name: What it actually scores
chapters.narration: Scoring is pure geometry: head forward, trunk lean, head tilt, and shoulder level angles, checked against a depth gate. A local dashboard shows the live skeleton, so you can verify tracking and tune camera placement.
bullets: Posture scored from head and shoulder geometry, gated by depth
A chime first, then a spoken prompt while the slouch persists
A local web dashboard with the live skeleton overlay

chapters.name: From zero to dashboard
chapters.narration: Getting running is two commands, and setup ends with a hardware preflight report. Setup is idempotent, and every preflight line should read pass before the first run. Then one command serves the dashboard.
terminal: PASS  audio sinks — USB sound card

chapters.name: The nudge ladder
chapters.narration: Hold a slouch for two seconds and the chime fires once. Ten seconds later the spoken prompt fires, repeating at most every thirty seconds. Sit up straight for three seconds and everything goes quiet.
terminal: # chime plays, then the spoken prompt

chapters.name: Never nudges on bad data
chapters.narration: Nudges never fire on bad data. If landmark confidence or depth drops, the badge reads unreliable, and the system stays silent.
bullets: The person must sit inside the depth band to be scored
Landmark visibility must clear a floor before a score is trusted
Leave the desk, and the badge reads NO PERSON — silent

chapters.name: Tuning, not code
chapters.narration: Every threshold, duration, and audio sink lives in one config file. Chimes too eager? Raise the angle thresholds. Voice too chatty? Stretch the cooldown. All durations are seconds, and all angles are degrees.

chapters.name: No camera? No problem
chapters.narration: Without a RealSense attached, the pipeline falls back to a synthetic frame source, so the dashboard is fully verifiable before the camera is ever plugged in. The full test suite runs the same way.
